text:
anne_support: Customer (Highland Labs) filed a ticket — intermittent 504s from our hosted API when calling via JS SDK 3.4.1. They say it started after yesterday's client update. Error screenshot attached.

jordan_csm: Seen a correlated latency spike and billing alert (retry storms) around 11:02-11:10 UTC. Customer is on Dedicated but using hosted API key through the SDK.

tom_devex: Can you paste the error/stack and package.json? Also which OpenAPI spec commit was used to generate the SDK?

anne_support: Stack snippet: ```Error: Request failed with status code 504
    at settle (/workspace/node_modules/axios/lib/core/settle.js:19:12)
    at IncomingMessage.handleStreamEnd (/workspace/node_modules/axios/lib/adapters/http.js:260:11)
    at IncomingMessage.emit (events.js:400:28)
    at endReadableNT (internal/streams/readable.js:1336:12)
``` package.json: ```{"dependencies": {"@redwood/sdk": "3.4.1"}}``` Repro claims: tight loop hitting completions.

sara_infra: Noted. CI on the openapi repo shows a regen commit yesterday that tweaked retry header ordering and added a new optional header `x-redwood-retry`. Generated TS client ended up changing default retry/backoff behavior in a subtle way. Commit: 9f2b3e (openapi/specs).

tom_devex: That could explain cross-SDK drift — our generator stamp changed header marshaling and the TS template bumped retry semantics. Which other SDKs show it?

anne_support: Python client 2.9.0 customers reported similar 504s but far fewer retries. Go v1.8.0 looks unaffected (less aggressive retry defaults).

jordan_csm: Customer provided a tiny repro: single-process loop doing ~100 requests/sec to completions with default SDK config. They saw an invoice jump due to retries.

tom_devex: Repro simplified: ```for (let i=0;i<200;i++) { await client.completions.create({ prompt: 'x' }) }``` With JS default retries we may be retrying on 5xx/504 quickly and amplifying backend pressure. Suggest immediate opt-in change: lower default retries in JS SDK until we patch generator.

sara_infra: From infra side, there was an autoscaler lag on the Dedicated pool during that window. The regen made the client retry more eagerly (shorter backoff), amplifying the surge -> queue overflow -> 504s. I'm going to roll back the OpenAPI shim that reordered retry headers to stop the behavior spreading.

ci-bot: CI: openapi-regen job failed diff check — spec change modified `x-redwood-retry` header placement and default `retry` parameter. https://ci.internal/redwood/openapi/12345 (logs attached)

tom_devex: Action items: 1) Patch JS SDK (publish 3.4.2) to conservative retry defaults and expose config; 2) Revert the regen change in openapi/specs and re-run client generation; 3) Run cross-sdk smoke tests (python/js/go) against a staging Dedicated pool; 4) Approve customer billing adjustment for retry-related spike. I'll open PRs for 1 & 2.

anne_support: I told the customer a temporary workaround: pin Python client (2.9.x) or set `client.options.retries = 0` for JS while we push the patch. They accepted a partial refund and asked for ETA.

jordan_csm: Please cc me on the PRs and include a short postmortem blurb for the customer. They want assurance this won't recur. :thumbsup:

tom_devex: Will do. Quick note: add a CI gate that runs a tiny load test on regen changes to catch retry/backoff regressions in future.

anne_support: Thanks — I'll update the support ticket with the plan and ETA.

jordan_csm: Appreciate the fast triage team.
